interview.question: How would you pick Axle's next country for home flexibility?
answer: Score markets on rules, device base, revenue per device and grid partner access.
At NESO I saw how market rules shape flexibility revenue and entry timing.
Use Cornwall Insight style due diligence; pilot with one supplier before scaling.

learn.title: Germany's §14a rules for controllable devices
bullets: §14a is a German rule for controllable home devices like EV chargers and heat pumps.
Grid operators may limit these devices in a grid emergency, down to a minimum power.
In return, owners get reduced grid fees, which shapes how flexibility software earns.
learn.so_what: Germany is a likely early Axle market, so knowing §14a shows you understand its device rules.

moves.text: Read the NESO locational ancillary services proposal; note how it could open new revenue for home devices.

takeaways.text: NESO plans location-based buying of ancillary services, so local flexibility could pay more in GB.
US states are forcing utilities to run virtual power plants, so new markets are opening.
Levelise adds Hinen batteries to its VPP, so competitors keep widening device support.

top3.headline: NESO proposes locational ancillary services buying
bullets: NESO has set out proposals to buy ancillary services by location.
Details are in Utility Week; the paywall may limit full reading.
top3.why: Location-based pricing could reward home devices in constrained areas, changing Axle's GB revenue model.
top3.use: Use your NESO background to discuss how locational signals affect flexibility revenue in interviews.

top3.headline: New Jersey must launch virtual power plants
bullets: Utilities have under a year to implement PowerUp NJ.
The two-year interim scheme will inform a long-term open-access VPP tariff.
top3.why: A new US state VPP programme could become a pilot market for home flexibility firms.
top3.use: Cite this as proof that US regulators are pushing virtual power plants into the mainstream.

top3.headline: Levelise adds Hinen batteries to its VPP
bullets: Hinen home batteries now work with Levelise's energy management platform.
They can join Levelise's Virtual Power Plant (VPP) through installers.
top3.why: A UK competitor is widening device support, which is the same race Axle is in.
top3.use: Add Levelise to your competitor map; expect an interview question on it.

top3.headline: Italy decree may cut battery revenues
bullets: A new market decree could reduce price spikes in Italy.
Grid-scale battery revenues may fall in 2027 and 2028 only.
top3.why: Italy is a possible Axle market, and lower price spikes would reduce flexibility revenue.
top3.use: Mention Italy's price-spike risk when discussing how you would model revenue per device.
